For each integer \(n\ge2\), let \(F_n\) be the free group on \(n\) generators. For any group \(G\), define its lower central series by \(\gamma_1(G)=G\) and \(\gamma_{r+1}(G)=[\gamma_r(G),G]\), where \([H,K]\) is the subgroup generated by the commutators \([h,k]=hkh^{-1}k^{-1}\) with \(h\in H\) and \(k\in K\). For every integer \(r\ge1\), define
\[
\mathcal A_r(n)=\ker\!\left(\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}\bigl(F_n/\gamma_{r+1}(F_n)\bigr)\right),
\qquad \operatorname{IA}_n=\mathcal A_1(n).
\]
Determine, by explicit conditions on \(n\) and \(c\), the complete set
\[
\mathcal D=\left\{(n,c)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge2}\times\mathbb Z_{\ge1}:\ 
\gamma_{c+1}(\operatorname{IA}_n)\subsetneq
\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\cap\mathcal A_{c+1}(n)
\right\}.
\]

content.text:
This asks for a classification that is **not currently known**: it is a graded form of the Andreadakis problem.

To see the connection, put \(H=F_n/\gamma_2(F_n)\). The degree-\(c\) Johnson homomorphism restricts to a map
\[
J_c:\frac{\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)}
{\gamma_{c+1}(\operatorname{IA}_n)}
\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}
\left(H,\frac{\gamma_{c+1}(F_n)}{\gamma_{c+2}(F_n)}\right).
\]
Here one uses the standard inclusion
\(\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\subseteq\mathcal A_c(n)\).
Its kernel is exactly
\[
\ker J_c=
\frac{\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\cap\mathcal A_{c+1}(n)}
{\gamma_{c+1}(\operatorname{IA}_n)}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
(n,c)\in\mathcal D\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad J_c
\text{ is not injective}.
\]
The noninjectivity degrees of these maps have not been completely classified.

Some established facts illustrate the situation:

* **Rank two:** \(\operatorname{IA}_2=\operatorname{Inn}(F_2)\), and its lower central series agrees with the Andreadakis filtration. Thus
  \[
  (2,c)\notin\mathcal D\qquad(c\ge1).
  \]
* **Degree one:** the abelianization theorem for \(\operatorname{IA}_n\) gives
  \[
  \mathcal A_2(n)=[\operatorname{IA}_n,\operatorname{IA}_n],
  \]
  so \((n,1)\notin\mathcal D\).
* **A known counterexample:** Bartholdi’s rank-three computation gives a nonzero degree-six kernel, yielding
  \[
  (3,6)\in\mathcal D.
  \]

Moreover, if for a fixed \(n\) none of the pairs \((n,c)\) belonged to \(\mathcal D\), induction would give
\(\mathcal A_c(n)=\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\) for every \(c\): whenever equality holds at degree \(c\), absence from \(\mathcal D\) gives equality at degree \(c+1\).

Thus the requested complete explicit conditions go beyond the known results:
\[
\boxed{\text{A complete determination of }\mathcal D\text{ is an open problem.}}
\]

Then, since the Andreadakis filtration is descending,
\[
\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\cap\mathcal A_{c+1}(n)
=\mathcal A_c(n)\cap\mathcal A_{c+1}(n)
=\mathcal A_{c+1}(n).
\]

 # Central crossed covers and lower-central detectors

Let A=<S|R> be a finitely presented group, N a finitely generated normal subgroup generated by images of Y={y_1,...,y_m}. Suppose explicit words W_y(S) give those images, and endomorphisms sigma_s,sigma_sinv of F(Y) give the actual conjugation actions of s,s^{-1} on N.

Define H=F(Y)/M, where M is the smallest normal subgroup invariant under every sigma_s and sigma_sinv and containing:
(1) inverse-action relations sigma_s sigma_sinv(y)y^{-1} and sigma_sinv sigma_s(y)y^{-1};
(2) action consistency sigma_r(y)y^{-1} for r in R;
(3) Peiffer relations sigma_Wy(z) (y z y^{-1})^{-1} for y,z in Y.
All of these are true relations in N. In H, the substitutions are automorphisms, satisfy R, and hence define an A-action. The map f:H->N is equivariant and surjective. Peiffer identities on generators imply f(h) dot a = h a h^{-1} for every h,a in H, where dot denotes the left A-action. Thus if f(h)=1, Inn(h)=identity: ker f is central in H.

## Graded central-kernel lemma

For any surjection f:H->N with central kernel K, the kernel of gr_gamma(H)->gr_gamma(N) is contained in the center of gr_gamma(H). Indeed if x in gamma_c(H) maps into gamma_{c+1}(N), surjectivity gives x=z k for z in gamma_{c+1}(H),k in K. Then [x,H] is contained in gamma_{c+2}(H), proving its graded class brackets trivially with every degree-one class, hence with the entire generated graded Lie ring.

## Conditional all-degree torsion detector

Suppose a torsion class t in gr_d(H) admits iterated brackets t_k=[...[t,x_1],...,x_k] nonzero for arbitrarily large k, with each x_j in gr_1(H). Every t_k is torsion. If some t_k maps to zero in gr(N), then its centrality forces t_{k+1}=0 and all later brackets zero, a contradiction. Thus every t_k survives in gr(N). When N=IA_n, every torsion class maps to zero under the integral Johnson homomorphism, whose target is free abelian. This proves strictness in every corresponding degree.

The lemma does NOT by itself produce such a torsion tower or establish rank stabilization. Those are still required. It avoids the stronger and unnecessary demand that the finite invariant cover H be exactly IA_n or that all identities among GL_n quotient relators be known. Its construction is an invariant L-presentation with explicit finite seed relators and substitutions.

### 1. The counterexample

Write \(F_3=\langle x,y,z\rangle\). Define automorphisms fixing generators not explicitly mentioned:
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
a:x\mapsto yxy^{-1},& b:x\mapsto zxz^{-1},\\

\]
All belong to \(\operatorname{IA}_3\). With the problem’s commutator convention, put
\[
u=[ [a,e],m]^3
  [[a,m],e]^{-1}
  [[a,b],b]^{-4}
  [[b,m],d]^{-2}.
\]
Plainly \(u\in\gamma_3(\operatorname{IA}_3)\). The team proved
\[
u\in\mathcal A_4(3),\qquad
u\notin\gamma_4(\operatorname{IA}_3).
\]

### 2. Why \(u\in\mathcal A_4(3)\)

The standard central-filtration property gives
\(\gamma_r(\operatorname{IA}_n)\subseteq\mathcal A_r(n)\). The degree-\(r\) Johnson map records the action modulo \(\mathcal A_{r+1}\), with values in degree-\(r\) derivations of the free Lie ring; it respects brackets.

Number the relevant Magnus generators as
\[
(g_0,g_1,g_2,g_3,g_5)=(a,b,m,d,e),
\]
and let \(D_{ijk}=[[D_i,D_j],D_k]\), where \(D_i\) is the first Johnson derivation. The exact integral identity is
\[
3D_{052}-D_{025}-4D_{011}-2D_{123}=0.
\]
It is precisely the degree-three Johnson image of \(u\).

A short hand verification was obtained. In the free Lie ring set
\[
k=[x,y],\quad w=[y,z],\quad h=[x,z],
\]
\[
P=[[k,z],z],\quad Q=[[w,z],x],\quad
R=[w,h],\quad S=[[h,z],y],\quad T=[[w,y],z].
\]
The derivations \(D_{052},D_{025},D_{011},D_{123}\), listed by their values on \((x,y,z)\), are respectively
\[
(-P+Q-R,T,0),\quad(-S-R,T,0),\quad
(Q,0,0),\quad(-P,T,0).
\]
Jacobi and Leibniz give \(S=P+Q+2R\), proving the identity.
